A1.justification: Both PDFs describe InterDyn and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material. Renamed comparisons and material moved between the main text and appendices can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original CLEVRER generations, quantitative SSV2 comparisons, and DexYCB control-signal experiments, including results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds video-baseline comparisons, additional metrics, and evaluation on SSV2 pretending actions.

M1.justification: The frozen SVD backbone, trainable temporal ControlNet branch, image/mask conditioning, and training framework remain. v2 clarifies the copied encoder and connections to the frozen decoder; this documents the architecture more precisely without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: CLEVRER, SSV2 with Something-Else annotations, and DexYCB are retained. v2 Appendix C adds explicit evaluation on pretending actions excluded from training, extending action-scenario coverage. Newly disclosed filtering of the retained SSV2 experiments does not establish that their underlying coverage changed.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands the video comparison from two CosHand variants to include Seer and DynamiCrafter, substantially broadening comparison beyond extensions of a static-state method. The CosHand variants are renamed and retained; the static comparator set is unchanged in v1 Table 2 versus v2 Table S1.

E3.justification: v2 adds FID, KID, and KVD to the existing metrics. New video baselines receive an initial image and SSV2 class-label instruction; DynamiCrafter receives distributional evaluation without frame-aligned metrics. The new pretending evaluation uses 828 or 1,156 samples depending on resolution; retained training settings are not shown to have changed.

E4.justification: The new pretending-class test examines generalization to actions excluded from training and reports lower motion fidelity with similar image-quality scores. The existing DexYCB control-type, occlusion, and resolution ablation moves from appendix Tables 3–4 to main-text Table 2 without new results. Per-class analysis and failure examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point scores without repeated-run counts, seed variation, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional KID/KVD scores are evaluation metrics rather than new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands reported findings while retaining the original shared scores. Table 1 adds Seer and DynamiCrafter results, including FVD 287.46 and 204.11, and new distributional scores showing CosHand-Independent's FID advantage: 2.95 versus InterDyn's 4.95/5.07. Table S2 adds pretending-action results. Static, DexYCB, and per-class numerical results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 Eq. (2) introduces an undefined factor a into the x-displacement product, changing the printed correlation definition and creating a mathematical defect absent in v1. This does not establish an implemented metric change. No new theoretical derivations or proofs are added.

C1.justification: v2 removes the introduction's claim that InterDyn is the first framework of its kind, narrowing its novelty claim. The central contributions remain controllable continuous and post-interaction dynamics without explicit reconstruction or simulation, generalization to unseen objects, and superiority over static-state baselines.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies image-quality superiority with the FID/KID exceptions and proposes frozen-backbone and spatial-prior explanations. It adds qualifications about inconsistent post-interaction dynamics and sample-size-dependent distributional comparisons. It also removes v1's assurance that difficult-action failures are not inherent limitations and compresses detailed failure explanations.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands SSV2 construction and evaluation documentation: excluded classes, visibility/size/length filtering, object-centered cropping, and resolution-specific training/validation counts. It additionally specifies 50-step Euler inference and 80GB H100 memory. Some details are removed, including CosHand's latent-space rollout explanation and the Diffusers pointer. These are documentation changes, not evidence of rerunning retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Seer, GroundingDINO, FID, and KID, and removes the Diffusers entry. Positioning expands to language-instructed video prediction and drops the first-framework claim, while the broader related-work organization remains. Numerous publication and formatting updates concern already-cited works.

P1.justification: Method and experiment exposition is extensively reorganized into clearer task, backbone, control, inference, dataset, and analysis paragraphs. The control ablation moves into Section 4.5, static comparison moves into the appendix, and supplementary sections are restructured, including removal of Ethical Considerations. These changes substantially revise the document's narrative organization.

P2.justification: v2 adds a pipeline diagram, expands Table 1, merges the two DexYCB tables, and adds Table S2. It redesigns the CLEVRER display while removing ground-truth sequences, rearranges control-signal illustrations, and splits the class-ranking table into two panels. Several retained figures and tables are relocated; most generated examples remain the same.

improvement.justification: Broader video comparisons, metrics exposing CosHand's strengths, the pretending-action test, and clearer data/inference documentation improve evaluation and transparency. These gains are moderated by removal of CLEVRER ground-truth comparisons, shorter failure explanations, and the unexplained symbol in Eq. (2). The evidence supports a limited net quality improvement, with physics validation still primarily qualitative.
